purpose: control changes to systems and processes so each one is assessed, approved by the right person, scheduled and reversible
entry_criteria: A change process and approval roles are defined
A record of the systems and owners exists
procedure: Record each change with what, why, who, systems affected and the planned time.
Classify by risk using the written criteria: standard (pre-approved), normal or emergency.
Assess the impact, including dependencies, users affected, test results and the rollback plan.
Route the request to the named human approver for its class; an agent prepares the pack but does not approve.
Check the calendar for clashes, apply the change in the approved window and record the outcome.
Review failed and emergency changes afterwards and feed the lessons back into the criteria.
deliverables: approval record with a human name
acceptance_criteria: Each change has a risk class and a rollback plan
A named human approved normal and emergency changes
validation_method: Named change approver; emergency changes reviewed afterwards.

validation.check: sample ten recent changes and check each has a risk class, rollback plan and approver name
compare production changes seen in deploy logs with change records

failure_modes.detection: Deploy log entry has no change
failure_modes.response: Raise it as an incident and record retrospectively

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A database index change is classed as normal; the approver asks for the rollback script to be tested in staging, schedules it in the quiet window, and the outcome is recorded with the measured query time.
